Exploratory gripper control · 28 October 2026 · one fresh seed

Official FlashSAC cable gripper control

Pristine authors’ compiled Torch FP16 AMP learner with the same three-step returns and 96,000-update learning-rate horizon in both runs.

Study question. What happens when only gripper action dimension 7 gains a factor of 3, while seven relative arm coordinates retain gain 1? The separately audited reference and fresh control each collect 49,152,000 transitions with the same seed 2 initial model and nine checkpoints on 128 common physical states. Replay/log-density coordinates remain normalized. The fresh stochastic trajectories differ; one seed does not establish a causal mechanism or a reliable rescue.

Observed outcome. Neither the gain 1 reference nor the gripper gain 3 control demonstrated cable pickup under the common evaluation. All nine saved checkpoints in each run recorded 0% goal attainment, final hold and lift. A higher return alone does not establish pickup.

Ever goal means segment 6 came strictly within 5 cm of its commanded XYZ. Occupancy uses the full 128×150 episode-step budget. Final hold requires the last 15 steps within goal; lift separately means middle-segment height exceeded 5 cm. These geometry metrics do not confirm contact or grasp. Clean timeout is horizon survival without an early failure; survival and return do not establish pickup. No population task-solved threshold is introduced.

Physical evaluation and stochastic training

All evaluations use full cable gravity −9.81 m/s² and final action-rate penalty −0.1, including checkpoint 0. Training retains stock gravity and action-rate curricula. Both runs record stochastic collection geometry, including warmup and autoresets; world-ever fractions are not per-episode evaluation success. Survival and return are reported separately from lift, goal and hold.

Training geometry events. Gripper gain 3 control · seed 2: 2 of 2000 iterations contained any world above the 5 cm lift threshold; the largest world fraction in one iteration was 0.0977%, and peak middle-segment height was 6.67 cm. Goal events occurred in 0 iterations. Gain1 reference · seed 2: 0 of 2000 iterations contained any world above the 5 cm lift threshold; the largest world fraction in one iteration was 0.0000%, and peak middle-segment height was 3.48 cm. Goal events occurred in 0 iterations. Each iteration covers 1,024 worlds × 24 steps and can span resets. The count describes positive training iterations; the fraction counts worlds with any event within one iteration. These are not unique episode counts or sustained holds. A brief height excursion is a geometric proxy, without contact/grasp proof or evidence of sustained learning.

Update, action and reward evidence

Alpha is an entropy loss coefficient rather than a direct action-noise multiplier. Negative differential entropy is valid. The 8-action Gaussian-reference sigma 0.15 gives target −3.82545 nats, not a measured rollout standard deviation. Historical discounted-return moments and maximum reward magnitude determine adaptive reward scaling; interaction with curricula is a hypothesis, not an established cause. Critic support saturation is not established by the logged losses.

Observed execution costs

Both fresh processes follow their allocation’s selected official smoke. Export policies differ: the gain 1 pilot archives full final replay plus learner state; this control archives only 8,192 fixed replay samples. Total-wall speed ratios are therefore omitted. Parent training/evaluation clocks and nested loop, collection, learning and checkpoint costs retain their actual scopes. Host collection includes inference, bridge, physics, Torch MDP and replay insertion; learning includes update APIs and waits. GPU/cache, resets and trajectories can differ, so these are not isolated kernel timings.

Action, recipe and artifact limits

Both learning recipes retain n3, architecture, losses, 10M learning replay, 100,000 warmup, batch 2,048, gamma 0.99, peak 3e-4 and floor 1.5e-4. Each optimizer advances its pristine scheduler on attempted updates, including AMP skips, against the same 96,000 horizon; actor/temperature update half as often. Seven arm targets remain q_current+0.03×a. The stock gripper mapping is q_finger=0.02×(clip(g×a7,−1,1)+1)m, with g=1 or 3. This changes endpoint occupancy plus last-action observations and action-rate inputs; it does not change normalized replay or loss coordinates. Finger-joint sums and command signs are geometry/control proxies, not grasp or fingertip-contact proof.

All nine portable actor/critic/target/Adam/scaler/scheduler/reward-normalizer checkpoints are retained. Smoke uses its full smaller replay for reload checks. The control’s final production export contains four prespecified 2,048-transition samples only, not all 10M entries, pending batches, global RNG or simulator state. No full-production replay, exact-resume or native n3 parity claim is made. Replay samples cannot reconstruct transition age or prove coverage of unsampled storage.
